_comment: Adversarial perturbations of compile-smoke. Every case here is a smoke case with
its pinned OUTPUT perturbed, not its input brief — with a pinned provider the
brief never reaches a model, so perturbing it would test nothing. Gates run on
output, so output is where an adversary has leverage.
Expectations encode DESIRED behaviour, not measured behaviour. That is deliberate
and it is the opposite of what a regression suite normally does. Recording the
current PASS as expected would make the suite protect the weakness: fixing the
gate would then break the build. So a case that is currently evaded FAILS, and
eval/adversarial-known-evasions.json carries it with a reason — under the same
stale rule as scripts/catalog-known-defects.json. An evasion that starts being
caught makes its entry stale, and a stale entry fails.
Why this suite exists at all: the differential oracle compares the TS gates against
the frozen Python linter, and ADR-0007 says plainly that parity is structurally
blind to a defect both implementations share. Five of the evasions below are that
kind of defect. The oracle cannot find them, by construction. This corpus is the
